Elaine / team — sharing the test summary and recommended tunables. Full CSV attached (concurrency-results-20260730.csv). Quick summary first, then methodology and recommended actions.

Summary (test harness: Redwood dedicated pool, n1-standard, GPT-like 13B sim):
- Workload profile: interactive chat flow, mean tokens per request = 120, median sequence length = 80.
- Burst test: sustained 30s bursts at 900 req/min (15 RPS) from 10 clients = peak concurrency ~150 active requests; observed p95 latency = 420 ms, p99 = 780 ms, mean TTFT = 310 ms. Queueing observed when backlog > 60 requests.
- Steady-state test: 30-minute steady at 200 req/min (3.3 RPS) = avg concurrency ~35; observed p95 latency = 160 ms, p99 = 320 ms, mean TTFT = 140 ms.
- Throughput ceiling (single model slot): safe continuous throughput ~ 240 req/min before latencies degrade >20% vs baseline.

Queueing & backpressure notes:
- When backlog exceeds 50–60 requests the runtime begins to batch larger groups which reduces per-request overhead but increases individual TTFT for early requests in the batch — visible as a tail.
- If the gateway allows unlimited inflow, latency can step up in a stair-step pattern as queue depth crosses batching thresholds.

Recommended rate-limit settings (for VitaCore gateway):
- Soft limit: 220 req/min per model endpoint with a 10 req/min reserve for bursts. Enforce token-bucket with refill every 1s and burst allowance of 30 tokens.
- Hard limit: 280 req/min (reject) to prevent large backlog. Return 429 with Retry-After when hard limit hit.
- Backoff guidance: exponential retry with jitter starting at 100ms should smooth retry storms.

Autoscale & config tips:
- Configure autoscale to add one extra slot when moving from steady-state to sustained bursts > 60s. For short bursts (<45s), prefer soft queuing + burst allowance.
- Turn on prefix KV caching for repeated prompts to reduce token count on warmed sessions (measured ~12% cost reduction in these runs).

Attachments: concurrency-results-20260730.csv (run-level datapoints), latency-p95-graph.png (PNG chart)

Methodology (brief):
- 3 runs per profile, warm-up 5 minutes, consistent seed prompts, measured client-side TTFT and server-side token timings, no model degradation induced.

If you want, we can re-run with VitaCore traffic shape (you can share a 1-hour sample of request timestamps and token counts) — should be a quick additional run.

-Dylan
